note: Generated by diffsim/src/corpus/avm_corpus_programs.test.ts. `bytes` and `address` are asserted equal to upstream's C++ BytecodeBuilder output as recorded in fixtures/wasm-parity/native-with-roots.results.

add.intent: The canonical smoke program: ADD two U32s and RETURN. Four instructions. If this one diverges native-versus-wasm then nothing else in the corpus is worth reading, which is exactly what a smoke program is for.

revert.intent: A deliberate REVERT_8. It exists to exercise the throw/catch revert path, which is the single thing wasi-sdk 27 cannot compile: under barretenberg`s BB_NO_EXCEPTIONS shim (`#define try if(true)`) any C++ exception in a wasm build silently becomes std::abort(), so a revert would look like a crash rather than a revert. This program is the fixture behind M4.

loop.intent: 64 unrolled iterations of MUL/ADD over U64. Exercises the interpreter over a real instruction count rather than a handful, with tag checking and per-instruction gas accounting on every step, so a gas-table or tag-semantics divergence has somewhere to show up.

sha256.intent: SHA256COMPRESSION over 8 state words and 16 input words. Pulls a real crypto gadget into the executed path: a gadget that miscompiles for wasm32 (32-bit shifts, endianness, unaligned loads) is completely invisible to arithmetic-only programs, and this is the cheapest program that would catch it.

poseidon2.intent: POSEIDON2PERM — the hash the protocol itself is built on, and the one every merkle domain separator feeds. A divergence in this permutation is a divergence in every tree root in the system, so it is the highest-value single gadget in the seven.

storage.intent: SSTORE of a field to a slot, then a return. The only one of the seven that reaches the merkle DB and moves the public-data tree, which is why its end-public-data root differs from every other program in the native-versus-wasm transcript. Without it the tree-root lines in that transcript would be seven copies of the same constant.

burn.intent: A tight 16-instruction ADD body with a backward JUMP_32, running until it exhausts the gas limit — 38,903 instructions executed. Two jobs: it gives instructions-per-second on identical work for native versus wasm, and it is the only one of the seven whose halt is out-of-gas rather than RETURN or REVERT, so the out-of-gas path is covered by the transcript at all.
